correctness.rationale: For each admissible finite-length continuum choose a contact point in each disk. A finite-length planar continuum is rectifiably arcwise connected: take an arc from contact 1 to 2 and the part of an arc from contact 3 to 1 up to its first hit on the first arc. Splitting there gives three segments of arcs with disjoint interiors, each of length at least the distance from the junction to the corresponding disk (coincident contacts permit a zero arm). Conversely, three nearest-disk projections of a junction give a connected feasible star of length at most the sum. This proves the global distance-sum reduction, with attainment by coercivity. Convexity and reflection put a minimizer on the axis, and projection to [0,h] cannot increase distances. The single-point covering radius is obtained by balancing the increasing base distance sqrt(1+y²) and decreasing apex distance h−y, with the minimizer at y=0 when h≤1. Below R(h), if r≥h then r<1 and the objective is 2(sqrt(1+y²)−r), minimized at y=0; this handles the degenerate clamp interval separately. Otherwise a_r≤h−r (strict if r>1, since r+sqrt(r²−1)<h). Below a_r the apex term decreases alone, above h−r the base term increases alone, and on [a_r,h−r] the derivative has its sole zero at c=1/sqrt(3). Hence the clamp formula. The apex arm first vanishes at r=h−c if c<h<sqrt(3); the base arms first vanish at r=2/sqrt(3) if h>sqrt(3); at equality the thresholds coincide with collapse. If r reaches h below R(h), the two remaining spokes become horizontal. For h≤c there is no positive-radius tripod. These give all rows including h=c,h=1,h=sqrt(3) and their endpoint equalities.
residual_risks: The phrase that both terms are active throughout the clamp interval should not be applied at r>h: that interval is the singleton {0}, where the apex term is zero. Treating it separately gives the same stated formula.

value.rationale: This natural three-site model retains an actual topology change, unlike a pure pointwise Steiner computation. The closed two-parameter formula and sharp exact thresholds distinguish whether the apex arm disappears, both base arms disappear, or all arms disappear together, and give benchmarks past the known short-radius regime. The shape examples alone would not be a distinct contribution.
residual_risks: Restricted to isosceles data and uniform radius; it neither classifies all optima nor all three-site geometries.
